question:
I have a common jinja macro for checking array of strings and return 0 or 1 based on that. But when i pass a single element inside an array( it is not going as array of string )

sample code:

{{ test_macro('code', ('02')) }} some_f

Macro code:

{% macro test_macro(
  col_name=column_name,
  codes=list_of_codes
) %}
{{ log("Codes:" ~ codes, True) }}
    case
      when {{ col_name }} in {{ codes }} then 1
      else 0
    end
{% endmacro %}

Compiled code is something like this

case
      when code in 02 then 1
      else 0
end

instead of

case
      when code in ('02') then 1
      else 0
end
title: passing single element inside array to jinja macro
answer:
Your approach will always return the compiled code you shared, even if the list of strings that you pass has more than one value.

One option that you have is to change the macro with the following:

{% macro test_macro(col_name, codes=[]) %}

    case
      when {{ col_name }}
        {%- if codes|length > 1 %}
          in (
          {%- for code in codes -%}
            '{{ code }}'
            {%- if not loop.last -%}
              ,
            {%- endif -%}
            {%- if loop.last -%}
              )
            {%- endif -%}
          {% endfor %}
        {% else %}
          = {{ codes[0] }}
        {%- endif %}
          then 1
      else 0
    end

{% endmacro %}

So that when you run the macro like this: {{ test_macro('code', ['2']) }}

It will compile as:

    case
      when code
          = 02
          then 1
      else 0
    end

Whereas if you add more codes, as in: {{ test_macro('code', ['2', '3']) }}

dbt will compile as:

    case
      when code
          in ('2','3')
        then 1
      else 0
    end

Note that, when calling the macro, you will need to enclose your second argument (the codes) in brackets.
